expected.startEvent: The principal dharma protector of Tibetan Buddhism, regarded in many Tibetan traditions as a wrathful manifestation of Avalokiteśvara, known in more than seventy-five forms and generally called simply mGon po, the Lord.

sources.reference: Reference treatment of Mahakala, Nagpo Chenpo, 'the Great Black One', regarded in many Tibetan traditions as a wrathful manifestation of Avalokitesvara, the bodhisattva of compassion: more than seventy-five forms are known in Tibet, where he is generally called mGon po, 'Master', 'Lord' or 'Protector'; the six-armed White Mahakala (Gonpo Karpo Chagdrugpa, Shadbhuja Sita Mahakala) is the most popular of these variations and is a wealth deity across all the traditions; his multiple arms are read as his capacity to carry out numerous tasks simultaneously.
